scope: Bounded static CPU-history check of already extracted DS1522+ firmware modules. No NAS access, UEFI variable read, whole-NVRAM read, credential/key variable inspection, target execution, or patch.

conclusion.historical_platform_recovery_from_curren: Not supported. AMD_PBS_SETUP stores current configuration flags and the DXE driver normalizes them to the current boot platform before registering its setup interface. A subsequent successful R1600 boot can overwrite the prior classification.
conclusion.go_no_go_impact: This path cannot remove the unknown V1500B platform selection or prove its final boot stage. Reading the current named variable would establish current stored flags only.
conclusion.amdsetup_history: No reliable historical CPUID/core-count/platform-ID record was established in the bounded AmdSetup check. Its name and persistence alone are not historical evidence; no NAS read is recommended for this purpose.

payload_fields.meaning: One derived flag from token 0x10000001. This is NOT a bit extracted from the actual platform-ID token.
A coarse current-platform group flag. Platform 0 yields 0; platform 8 yields 1. The value does not preserve the full platform ID or uniquely identify a CPU.
Configuration layout/version marker; old values below 0x28 trigger migration. It is not a CPU-history counter.

boot_write_chain.fact: Initialization is reached from the module entry, before the setup-form interface is registered. It does not require the user to enter the BIOS menu.
Read AMD_PBS_SETUP through 0x4188. Compare offsets 0 and 2 against the current PCD-derived expressions. On mismatch, update each field and set the write-required flag.
When data is missing, an old layout needs migration, or a current classification flag differs, call the persistent writer at 0x402c. A write failure propagates as an error.

For an existing variable, read its current size/data, replace the first 0x82 bytes with the supplied configuration, and SetVariable with attributes 7. If creating it, write a new 0x82-byte variable. This replaces current data; it does not append history.

pcd_identity_correction.fact: The inspected selection routine sets token 0x10000001 to 0, then writes the selected platform ID to token 0x10000000 and CPM main-table offset 0x31. Do not describe both PBS fields as platform-ID bits.

pei_consumer.fact: The earlier PEI routine reads these stored flags and checks them against the current tokens. Its local-buffer normalization is distinct from the later DXE persistent write proved above.

read_only_target_if_current_state_is_nee.api: UEFI GetVariable with this exact name and vendor GUID
read_only_target_if_current_state_is_nee.minimal_interpretation: Report the attributes and the first two uint16 fields. efivarfs prefixes variable data with a four-byte attribute header; API data does not include that header.
read_only_target_if_current_state_is_nee.availability: Requires working UEFI runtime-variable access in the current OS boot. No live availability or value was read in this task.
read_only_target_if_current_state_is_nee.historical_limit: Even a value of 0 or 1 at payload offset 2 describes current stored platform grouping after any successful normalization/write, not the CPU installed when the old failed boot occurred.

amdsetup.name: AmdSetup

bounded_observations.fact: Allocates a current setup buffer, calls the configuration loader at 0x958, and installs setup/configuration interfaces.
Reads AmdSetup, manages a fixed-sized current configuration and defaults, and may write the current buffer using SetVariable attributes 7. No historical event sequence was established.

amdsetup.limit: CPU identity and history semantics for every individual AmdSetup field were not established. Do not infer a historical V1500B boot from this variable or from a surviving setting. No broad variable enumeration or NVRAM recovery was performed.

limits: Static analysis establishes the writer and overwrite condition; it does not prove which fields were written during the historical failed V1500B run.
The overwrite conclusion assumes the subsequent R1600 boot reached this DXE driver and its SetVariable operation succeeded.
A zero result would not uniquely identify V1500B; other platform IDs below 8 yield the same flag.
No timestamps, previous-value archive, or CPUID/core-count historical log was established by this bounded investigation.
Deleted or stale flash-variable records were not searched and are outside this task.
